claim: Antitrust plaintiffs satisfy the predominance requirement for class certification by using a damages model that estimates damages attributable to the antitrust injury on a class-wide basis, only if individualized determinations are not needed to allocate damages among class members.
initial_reasoning: In Re Bystolic Antitrust Litigation held that a class can meet Rule 23(b)(3) predominance when the plaintiffs use a reliable damages model that attributes the antitrust injury to the class as a whole and no separate, individualized proof is required to apportion damages among members. This directly supports the claim’s description of the predominance requirement.
